task: t2 - make t53 recognise 'disconnected', correct the guide's expiry mechanism, add the third timestamp
headline: t53 now reports a dedicated BRIDGE_WINDOW_DISCONNECTED instead of the generic BRIDGE_CALL_FAILED when the editor says the window is disconnected (message or code). The guide's boundary 2 now states the real mechanism: /health can still say edaConnected:true while /execute returns 'EDA window ... disconnected', so availability must be probed with t53 or execute, not /health. The section carries three timestamps, the third copied verbatim from r7t5. The before/after here is a CLASSIFICATION-LEVEL verification, not a live reproduction: by the time I started, the window was fully gone (/health edaConnected:false, edaWindowCount:0), so the 'registered but disconnected' state could not be re-created.

verificationKind.why: The 'registered but disconnected' state does not exist any more. So the measured error string was fed into the real catch via an env-gated hook, and the gate's own exit code and reason were read back.

harness.whatItDoes: throws from the execute path so the same catch classifies it; skips discover() so a dead bridge cannot shadow the classification; bridge.execute is never called and the editor is never contacted
harness.whyItIsNecessary: execute is unreachable while discover() fails, and discover() fails whenever no window is registered - precisely the situation that made a live reproduction impossible
harness.disclosure: this is instrumentation, not behaviour: with the env var unset the gate runs exactly as before (verified by a plain run after the change: exit 2, reason BRIDGE_NO_EDA_WINDOW)

change2_httpApiSecondInstance.currentCode: const unavailable = /no eda window connected|not connected|no longer connected/i.test(message)
change2_httpApiSecondInstance.sameDisease: the editor's real wording is 'disconnected', which none of the three alternatives matches, so a dead window is answered with 500 (body failed) instead of 503 (unavailable)
change2_httpApiSecondInstance.worseThanThat: the comment directly above (L110-116) enumerates the phrasings it believes it covers, including `EDA window "…" is no longer connected. …`. The runtime message is `EDA window "…" disconnected`, so the comment is stale about the very string it exists to catch.
reasons: scope: the assignment says only t53 and the guide; http-api.mjs is relay source under packages/

a source edit would not change the running relay (long-lived process) without a restart, and a restart would tear down whatever registration state exists and disturb other members working in this workspace

the right fix is structural, not a second copy of the same regex: the error object already carries a machine code from bridge.ts (SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_WINDOW_LOST / SCHEMATIC_BRIDGE_DISCONNECTED). Status should be derived from the code and the message regex should only remain as a fallback. Patching a third phrasing in leaves the next wording change with the same bug.
change2_httpApiSecondInstance.proposedDiffNotApplied:
- const unavailable = /no eda window connected|not connected|no longer connected/i.test(message)
+ const unavailable = /no eda window connected|not connected|no longer connected|disconnected|window lost|no such window/i.test(message)
change2_httpApiSecondInstance.recommendedFollowUp: route on err.code first (WINDOW_LOST / DISCONNECTED / NO_EDA -> 503), keep the regex only as a fallback, and fix the stale L110-116 comment in the same change
